name: Slav Defense
description: Defend the d5 pawn with …c6, keeping the c8 bishop free to develop.

lines.name: Main Line (5.a4 Bf5)

notes.3: …c6 supports d5 without blocking the c8 bishop, unlike …e6.
notes.7: …dxc4 takes the pawn when White can't easily win it back with tempo.
notes.13: …Bb4 pins the c3 knight and stops White's e4 push.

5.Bf5: Qb3! hits b7, which the bishop no longer guards.

lines.summary: Take on c4, develop the bishop to f5 before …e6, then pin with …Bb4.

lines.name: 9.Qe2

notes.3: …c6 supports d5 without blocking the c8 bishop, unlike …e6.
notes.7: …dxc4 takes the pawn when White can't easily win it back with tempo.
notes.13: …Bb4 pins the c3 knight and stops White's e4 push.
notes.17: …Nbd7 prepares for e4 by covering e5.
notes.19: …Bg6 steps back from the pawn's attack, still eyeing e4.
notes.21: …Bh5 pins the f3 knight, so White's e5 push leaves d4 weaker.

5.Bf5: Qb3! hits b7, which the bishop no longer guards.

lines.summary: When White pushes e4, retreat the bishop to g6 and then pin with …Bh5.

lines.name: Krause (6.Ne5)

notes.3: …c6 supports d5 without blocking the c8 bishop, unlike …e6.
notes.7: …dxc4 takes the pawn when White can't easily win it back with tempo.
notes.11: …Nbd7 challenges the e5 knight right away.
notes.15: …e5 frees Black's game in the centre.

5.Bf5: Qb3! hits b7, which the bishop no longer guards.

lines.summary: Against 6.Ne5, challenge the knight with …Nbd7, then free your game with …Qc7 and …e5.

lines.name: 5.e4 b5

notes.3: …c6 supports d5 without blocking the c8 bishop, unlike …e6.
notes.7: …dxc4 takes the pawn when White can't easily win it back with tempo.
notes.9: …b5 holds on to the c4 pawn; Black gets queenside play against White's big centre.
notes.11: …Nd5: the knight is safe in the centre and eyes c3.

5.Bf5: Qb3! hits b7, which the bishop no longer guards.

lines.summary: Meet 5.e4 with …b5 to keep the pawn, then put the knight on d5 when it's kicked.

lines.name: 5.e4 b5 6.e5

notes.3: …c6 supports d5 without blocking the c8 bishop, unlike …e6.
notes.7: …dxc4 takes the pawn when White can't easily win it back with tempo.
notes.9: …b5 holds on to the c4 pawn; Black gets queenside play against White's big centre.
notes.11: …Nd5: the knight is safe in the centre and eyes c3.
notes.13: …e6 supports the d5 knight and opens the f8 bishop.
notes.19: …Bb7 guards d5 and the long diagonal; Black stays a pawn up.

5.Bf5: Qb3! hits b7, which the bishop no longer guards.

19.Be7: Nxf7! Kxf7 Qf3+ and Qxa8 wins the rook.

lines.summary: After 6.e5 Nd5 7.a4 e6, trade on c3, keep the b5 pawn and guard the long diagonal with …Bb7.

lines.name: 5.e4 b5 6.a4

notes.3: …c6 supports d5 without blocking the c8 bishop, unlike …e6.
notes.7: …dxc4 takes the pawn when White can't easily win it back with tempo.
notes.9: …b5 holds on to the c4 pawn; Black gets queenside play against White's big centre.
notes.11: …b4 kicks the knight away from the centre.
notes.13: …Nxe4 grabs the centre pawn while the a2 knight is out of play.

5.Bf5: Qb3! hits b7, which the bishop no longer guards.

lines.summary: When a4 hits the b5 pawn, push …b4 and take the e4 pawn while White's knight sits on a2.

lines.name: 5.e3 b5

notes.3: …c6 supports d5 without blocking the c8 bishop, unlike …e6.
notes.7: …dxc4 takes the pawn when White can't easily win it back with tempo.
notes.9: …b5 holds the extra c4 pawn for now.
notes.11: …b4 kicks the knight to a poor square on the rim.

5.Bf5: Qb3! hits b7, which the bishop no longer guards.

lines.summary: When White plays slowly with 5.e3, hold the pawn with …b5, then kick the knight with …b4.

lines.name: 4.Bg5 Bf5

notes.3: …c6 supports d5 without blocking the c8 bishop, unlike …e6.
notes.7: …Bf5 develops the bishop before the pin on f6 can bother Black.
notes.9: …e6 supports d5; if White takes on f6, Black has the two bishops.

5.Bf5: Qb3! hits b7, which the bishop no longer guards.

lines.summary: Against the early pin, develop with …Bf5 and …e6; Bxf6 gives you the two bishops.

lines.name: 3.Nf3 move order

notes.3: …c6 supports d5 without blocking the c8 bishop, unlike …e6.
notes.7: …dxc4: the same position as 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Nf3 dxc4.

lines.summary: 3.Nf3 and 3.Nc3 lead to the same main line: …Nf6, then …dxc4.

lines.name: Quiet 4.e3

notes.3: …c6 supports d5 without blocking the c8 bishop, unlike …e6.
notes.7: …Bf5: White's e3 shut in their own bishop, so Black gets this bishop out at once.
notes.11: …Bxd3 trades off White's best attacking bishop.
notes.13: …Nbd7 develops and prepares …Bd6 and a later …e5.

lines.summary: Against 4.e3, play …Bf5 at once, trade it on d3, then develop with …Nbd7.

lines.name: Exchange (3.cxd5)

notes.3: …c6 supports d5 without blocking the c8 bishop, unlike …e6.
notes.5: …cxd5 keeps a symmetrical, very solid pawn structure.
notes.9: …Nc6 develops and adds a defender to d4 and e5.

lines.summary: Symmetry is fine for Black: develop knights and bishop actively, then …e6.

lines.name: 8.Bd3

notes.3: …c6 supports d5 without blocking the c8 bishop, unlike …e6.
notes.5: …cxd5 keeps a symmetrical, very solid pawn structure.
notes.9: …Nc6 develops and adds a defender to d4 and e5.
notes.15: …Bxd3 trades bishops; the symmetrical position is very solid for Black.

lines.summary: Trade both pairs of bishops and castle; the Exchange Slav is then completely level.

lines.name: 8.Bb5

notes.3: …c6 supports d5 without blocking the c8 bishop, unlike …e6.
notes.5: …cxd5 keeps a symmetrical, very solid pawn structure.
notes.9: …Nc6 develops and adds a defender to d4 and e5.
notes.15: …Nd7 covers e5 and c5 and gets ready to chase the bishop with …a6.

lines.summary: Against the pin Bb5, play …Nd7 and be ready to ask the bishop with …a6.
